title: `sqlparse.split` does not treat T-SQL `GO` as a batch separator
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

In T-SQL scripts, `GO` on its own line separates batches, but `sqlparse.split` glues it onto the next statement.

```python
import sqlparse
sqlparse.split('USE foo;\nGO\nSELECT 1;\nGO')
```
Expected: `['USE foo;', 'GO', 'SELECT 1;', 'GO']`
Actual: `['USE foo;', 'GO\nSELECT 1;', 'GO']`

`GO` with a repeat count behaves the same: `sqlparse.split('USE foo;\nGO 2\nSELECT 1;')` should be `['USE foo;', 'GO 2', 'SELECT 1;']` but is `['USE foo;', 'GO 2\nSELECT 1;']`.

`GO`, optionally followed by a count, should end the current statement just like a `;` does, and be returned as its own statement.
acceptance: Both reported scripts split as expected
`GO` and `GO <n>` are returned as separate statements; existing `;` splitting is unchanged
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
